th month. Recorded by Yishan

The layman's name was Ruzhen, his courtesy name Jingshan, his style name Bao'an; he was a man of Fangqiao in Yuyao, Zhejiang. There were four brothers, and the layman was the youngest. In youth he studied the Confucian books; by nature he was mellow and good, filial in serving his parents, frugal and hardworking, loyal and honest without deceit. Grown to manhood he went into business, kindly in his dealings and resourceful in planning. At forty-two, moved by the turmoil of the nation's fortunes and the floating clouds of worldly affairs, he wished to abandon business altogether and give his whole mind to the Pure Land. But it was no easy thing to wind up the shop's affairs, and hard to shake off the dusty bonds, so he had no choice but to cultivate at home. He turned the shop into a lotus society, reciting the Buddha's name while carrying on business. He and his partners and their families all gave up wine and meat and devoted themselves to the pure karma. At every fifth watch he would recite the name of Amitabha several hundred times aloud, and so it went for nearly three years.

Since last summer his body had been weak and burdened with illness, lingering for more than a year. On the first day of the ninth month of this year he wrote inviting me to his home. Seeing his illness to be grave, I gave him a sharp warning: Why not put down the ten thousand conditions, refuse medicine and physicians, and recite the Buddha's name with one mind, seeking rebirth in the Pure Land? For one who recites the Buddha's name, to be able to recite in ordinary times is not so good as to be able to recite in illness. You have been ill a long time without recovery; what is there to fear in death? You should rather set your mind toward the Buddha's land, never parting from Amitabha in thought after thought, and vow to seek the Pure Land, never forgetting the Land of Bliss from moment to moment. Know deeply that the Saha world has many sufferings, and the Land of Bliss has immeasurable joy. Recite the Buddha's name with one mind, in the hope that Amitabha will receive you and bring you across to the other shore. The layman heard it and joyfully accepted. He at once refused medicine and physicians and all worldly bonds. And he had a note written out and pasted on the wall, to show all who came: I am resolved to recite the Buddha's name with one mind, to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, to leave the round of rebirth, and to end birth and death. All relatives and friends who visit my sickroom are earnestly begged not to talk of worldly matters, but to recite Amitabha the more, and help me toward rebirth in the Pure Land; my gratitude will be endless.

From then on, every day he asked several monks of the Guanzong Monastery to stay at his bedside and assist in reciting the Buddha's name, day and night without cease. On the morning of the eighth he suddenly saw Guanyin come and tell him: On the eighteenth you may reach the lotus assembly. The layman counted on his fingers and found there were still ten days; though he told others of it, in his heart he had not decided. On the fourteenth he saw Guanyin come again and say: On the eighteenth you will be born in the West; the date is exact. And so his mind was settled. He then told his son to write and urge me to come to Yuyao before the seventeenth, and to invite several more people who recite the Buddha's name to assist together in the recitation, seeing him off to the West. On the morning of the sixteenth he closed his eyes and saw the surpassing realm of the Land of Bliss, pure and adorned, present before his eyes. On the seventeenth he saw it again, and said: My birth in the West is certain. That day I set out from Ningbo and reached Yuyao at noon. I found his mind and spirit clear and fresh and all his faculties keen. Perfectly as usual, he said to me: I do not hang my heart on any of my affairs in the least, but my thought of being born in the West I never forget; perhaps I shall go at eleven tonight. The Dharma masters who assist in reciting the Buddha's name should rest more by day, for the night is hard work. Recite the Buddha's name the whole night through to help me. At nine that night, when the whole family and all the masters had gathered in the room reciting the Buddha's name, he himself called for a haircut, bathed, and changed his clothes

and when all was done he sincerely made his vow, lay quietly reciting the Buddha's name, and waited to be received. At twelve, when he did not see Amitabha come to welcome him, he raised his hand to count and changed the time to nine the next morning, saying to those present: I have good news: I see two boys carrying a pair of white silk lanterns, exceedingly bright. On the eighteenth, at eight in the morning, he asked for water to wash his face, and had his clothes and bedding set in order and his body laid straight; he lay quietly reciting the Buddha's name for half an hour, then suddenly stretched his hand out from the quilt, reverently joined his palms, and made the gesture of bowing to the Buddha three or four times. Then he gazed again at the image of Amitabha and told his son to face west and recite the Buddha's name. At twenty past nine he passed away at ease, wholly free of pain. Two hours later, when his whole body was felt, it was all cold, only the crown of his head exceedingly warm. His family all restrained their grief and recited the Buddha's name, and no sound of weeping was raised. At the encoffining his four limbs were soft and his face as in life. Reviewing all the layman's auspicious signs — foreknowing the time ten days beforehand, beholding the realm of the Land of Bliss in between, joining his palms in homage at the end, and the crown of his head growing cold last when his breath ceased — all are certain proof of his birth in the West.
(Original title: Old Mr. Wang Repeatedly Crying, Amitabha Buddha, Come Quickly and Save Me)

On the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month my younger sister sent someone to say that her uncle, old Mr. Wang, was gravely ill and asked me and my fellow brother-in-law Mr. Zhou Linpu to assist his recitation. When Mr. Zhou and I reached his home (in the village of Nizhi on Dai), the old man lay gasping on his sickbed and had already taken no food for three or four days. Seeing the two of us come, he joyfully joined his palms and bowed. Fearing that the old man's heart was heavy with love for his family, I made skillful means to exhort him: “Old uncle, you must recite the Buddha's name with one mind and seek rebirth in the West. Do not be tied to your family. Once you are tied, you cannot attain rebirth, and you will have to go to the hall of King Yama. Once in the underworld you lose your freedom and cannot look after your family at all. Only by being born in the West do you gain spiritual powers and perfect ease, so that you are not separated from this place even while separated. The worlds of the ten directions are still before your eyes — how much more your family and all those with whom you have karmic bonds? Therefore at this moment you must put everything down for the time being and strive for rebirth; only after rebirth is there any real possibility of looking after your family.” The old man said resolutely: “I will not bother about them anymore.” Afterwards, whatever exhortation was given he joyfully heard and accepted, his answers firm. Again and again he cried: “Amitabha Buddha, come quickly and save me.” That night they recited in shifts, and the sound of the Buddha-name was unbroken the whole night through.

On the morning of the twenty-seventh the suffering of his illness had melted away; he lay peacefully with closed eyes, quietly listening to the sound of the Buddha. From time to time his mouth moved slightly, as though reciting. At one in the afternoon his face suddenly turned outward, and amid the sound of Buddha-recitation he passed away in peace. Four hours later I felt his whole body; it had grown cold through, while the crown of his head was still warm. At half past nine that night, when they changed his clothes, his four limbs were soft and his face clear and moist; the whole family rejoiced, for this is certain proof of rebirth in the West.
, in the intercalary
th month, on the
th day. Respectfully recorded by Gu Huasun of Daishan, Dinghai
(Original title: Layman Yu Jingda, the Three Holy Ones Come to Welcome Him, and He Passes Away in Peace)

The layman's style name was Yecai and his Dharma name Jingda; his family had lived for generations in Nizhi village, Daishan, Dinghai. The family were farmers, and he was sincere and plain by nature. In dealing with others he was modest and self-effacing. He had a rough grasp of letters and loved to urge people to recite the Buddha's name. Later he joined the Right Faith Buddha-Recitation Society and took refuge under Great Master Xiufu, and hearing his instructions clearly he came to understand that the Pure Land Dharma gate of Buddha-recitation is a shortcut in cultivation. From then on he kept his lessons morning and evening, never breaking off in summer or winter, thinking of nothing but the Buddha and seeking nothing but the Pure Land.

Last winter he happened to catch a slight illness, but his mind was quite clear, and all day long he still chanted the Buddha-name aloud. By the fifteenth day of the first month of this spring, when I and Layman Mao Wujing and others went to inquire after his illness, we urged him with the principle of delighting in the Pure Land and loathing the Saha world, of taking up and letting go. The layman then cited the words of an ancient worthy: The three realms are like a cage, and my body is like a bird. For the flavors of the world I truly have no greed or attachment; but I regret that we country folk of this rustic place toil all day for food and clothing, and even with some cultivation have not attained one mind, and I fear rebirth in the West will be hard to hope for. Then Layman Yue Hongsong told him: Layman, do not misunderstand. You must know that the Pure Land Dharma gate is the supreme wondrous Dharma, all-pervading for the three capacities, wholly gathering in both the sharp and the dull. From the equal-enlightenment bodhisattvas above, who vow to seek rebirth, down to the perverse and evil ordinary man, for whom even ten recitations bring horizontal transcendence. Now you have cultivated for many years; you are not perverse or evil, and your merit exceeds ten recitations — how could you fail to be reborn? Then Layman Zhou Linpu told him of the actual proof of Mr. Yu Mingsheng of the same county, who attained rebirth with ten recitations. Hearing it, the layman said joyfully: Now that I have received this instruction, it is like building a high wall and laying a firm foundation, so that there is no more danger of collapse. All praised it as good, and assisted him in reciting the Buddha's name. At eight on the night of the twentieth the layman suddenly recited aloud the holy names of the two bodhisattvas Guanyin and Mahāsthāmaprāpta himself. Asked why, he said: Because I have already received the two bodhisattvas come to welcome me. Asked again whether he saw Amitabha Buddha, he said: He is seated on the golden terrace. Presently his breath came faster and faster, and amid the sound of Buddha-recitation he passed away in peace. It was

, the twentieth day of the first month, at the hour of xu; his worldly age was fifty-six. Eight hours later the crown of his head was still warm. On the twenty-second, when he was placed cross-legged in the shrine, his four limbs were soft as in life. Those who came from far and near to look all sighed that it was rare; such auspicious signs are indeed clear evidence of rebirth in the West. I have made this record of the facts in particular, wishing that those in the world who would escape the sea of suffering of birth and death may deeply believe that in the Pure Land Dharma gate ten thousand practice and ten thousand go, and that it cannot be compared with the other Dharma gates that rely wholly on one's own power.
Hong Minzhou

blocks.text: 28. The Three Holy Ones Come to Welcome Him

inline.s: (Original title: Layman Song Yunzhong, Golden Light Filling the Room, the Three Holy Ones Come to Welcome Him)

Layman Song Yunzhong loved painting from childhood, and at thirteen his father, Mr. Yulin, had him study under the famous painter Mr. Hang Jingying. The layman had a genius for art, studied with diligence besides, and his attainments were profound. Mr. Hang believed in the Buddha, and the layman was steeped in his influence. In the winter of the twenty-fifth year of the Republic, when Great Master Yinguang was expounding the Dharma at the Shanghai Dharma Assembly for Protecting the Nation and Averting Calamity, Mr. Hang led the layman and his fellow students to beg the Great Master to confer the three refuges; the layman received the Dharma name Zhen'gen, and was then twenty-one. He ate vegetarian food and recited the Buddha's name, keeping morning and evening lessons, his heart turned toward the pure realm. At twenty-six he married Miss Li Menghua, and entertained the guests with a vegetarian banquet at Gongdelin. Miss Menghua followed him in believing in the Buddha, and the couple were deeply devoted.

Two years ago the layman fell ill with his lungs and entered the hospital. For close to two years he was there, and seven ribs were removed, yet he was not cured. So he came home to nurse his illness, and recited the Buddha's name the more diligently. With the coming of winter his illness gradually grew grave. On the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month of this year I went to comfort him. The layman said: The suffering of illness is very great; when shall I return to the West? I said: In former days Dharma Master Xuanzang too suffered illness at the end, and a heavenly being told him: Master, for the karmic offenses of having harmed and vexed living beings through measureless kalpas, you now rely on the power of the Three Jewels and are turned to light recompense, and in this suffering of illness it is wholly finished. The layman's illness is likewise so. Amitabha's great vow says: “For the heavenly and human peoples of the worlds of the ten directions who in former lives did evil, if they hear my name, repent and do good, uphold the sutras and precepts, and vow to be born in my land, at the end of life they shall not pass through the three evil paths, but shall straightway come to be born there.” Therefore those whose evil karma in former lives was heavy and whose pure karma in this life is light receive the sufferings of illness before the end of life, to dissolve the evil karma, and at the end of life are born straight into the Land of Bliss. If their former evil karma was light and their pure karma in this life heavy, then before the end there is no more suffering of illness. This depends on whether a man can diligently cultivate the pure karma or not. Hence for a Buddhist to suffer illness at the end is precisely heavy recompense turned to light, a good omen before rebirth; the world does not understand it, and so falls into doubt and confusion — truly a mistake. What is called former life, this life, and the life to come is no other than yesterday, today, and tomorrow. This body comes driven by the power of the good and evil karma of former lives; while the recompense is not yet exhausted, how could it go? It is like a man who has business here: while the business is unfinished, how can he go elsewhere? Or like a prisoner whose term is not yet full: how can he leave prison? This body is the prison; the consciousness is the prisoner. When the prisoner's term is full, even if he wished to stay in prison, he could not. When the karmic recompense of this life is exhausted, the spirit-consciousness departs, and it cannot be kept. Layman, set your mind at ease and wait, holding the Buddha-name without forgetfulness. I also told his family: Where there is life there must be death, just as where there is day there must be night, going round and returning again — who can escape it? Though a life last a hundred years, in the end there must be parting. What is to be lamented is that after death each goes according to his karma to receive recompense, and there will be no set time for meeting again — that is what is pitiable. Now that Mr. Yulin and your worthy household can all recite the Buddha's name diligently, you shall afterward go together to the Land of Bliss and be companions in the Dharma forever, with no more parting; and so when this body of recompense is given up, it is rather a cause for rejoicing — why grieve? When the visit was finished I took my leave.

At ten that night his family had all gone to bed. The layman called out: Get up, get up! I am going to the West; please assist my recitation. The family gathered around the bed reciting the Buddha's name. The layman clapped his hands and called on Amitabha Buddha, telling the family to recite along. After a long while, he saw golden light fill the room and the Three Holy Ones of the West descend to welcome him; the layman then joined his palms, called on Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva once, and passed away. It was one in the morning of the twenty-ninth. Three days later, at the encoffining, his whole body was soft, and those who saw it sighed in wonder. The layman's whole family was steeped in the Buddha's transformation; his younger brother Yungong, eighteen this year, a graduate of the telecommunications college, serves the Buddha with especial diligence. The layman was a man of Jiading in Jiangsu, and lived at No. 202 Dongjiadu Street, Nanshi, Shanghai; his worldly age was twenty-nine.
, in the lunar
th month, on the
th day. Recorded by Chen Hailiang
(Original title: Old Mr. Zhang Youmei, Assisted in Recitation at the End, an Auspicious Rebirth)

To be reborn in the West and ascend to the stage of non-retrogression is a matter hard to encounter in a hundred thousand million kalpas. To die with the mind not inverted, in the auspicious sleeping posture, with the crown of the head warm at the end, is certain proof of rebirth in the West. Now here was a sixty-eight-year-old old man who had kept only the six vegetarian days, and only when gravely ill resolved to enter the lotus society and recite the Buddha's name; yet amid the sound of assisting recitation he obtained this rare auspicious sign. Was it that he had long since planted good roots under measureless millions of Buddhas? Or that the Pure Land Dharma gate is so supremely excellent that, beyond Chan, Vinaya, and Esoteric teachings, it displays this extraordinary efficacy? This must not go unrecorded, to strengthen the faith of those who are beginning to cultivate the Pure Land Dharma gate, and as an exhortation to those who do not know it.

Zhang Youmei was a man of Liushutou in the eastern district of Jiangyin. His family were scholars for generations, and Youmei also studied medicine. He was modest and gentle, and never haggled over the size of his fee; those who sought his treatment came one after another, and he had no leisure in the day. His village was about three li from Beiguo, and at Beiguo there was the Jigui Lotus Society. Youmei's eldest son, Mengliang, kept a vegetarian diet and served the Buddha, promoting the Lotus school with all his strength, and very many followed him in faith. Youmei at first clung obstinately to the Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu view of refuting the Buddha; then, from stories of karmic cause and retribution, he came to believe a little, and so kept the six vegetarian days.
, in the

th month he fell ill with quinsy, and the assembled physicians were helpless. He then had himself registered at the lotus society and named himself Juewu. He said that when his illness was cured he would enter the society and recite the Buddha's name. His son Mengliang, day after day, asked pure companions to recite the Buddha's name and release living creatures for him. He said that whenever he heard the sound of the Buddha he felt his mind grow clear. On the twelfth his illness grew grave. I said to him: Brother, now you must put everything down and silently recite Amitabha Buddha; Amitabha Buddha will naturally come to receive you. He could not speak, but nodded his head. At once his lips began to move, reciting the Buddha's name without cease. At that time in the next room the sound of the Buddha-name rang out clearly. Toward dusk he said: My mind is very clear now; the weather is hot, let everyone rest a while. On the thirteenth, at about six or seven in the afternoon, his illness grew more urgent, and I warned his wife and daughters not to weep before him and disorder his mind; for a son or daughter's first duty to a parent is to set his spirit at peace. Death is the most bitter thing in a human life, and one should let him not feel its bitterness but know only rebirth in the Land of Bliss. Then some twenty pure companions were gathered, and the four-character Buddha-name was raised aloud. At about ten, his whole body was cold; some three hours after his breath had ceased the Buddha-name was stopped and mourning begun, and his body still lay facing west in the auspicious posture. His friend felt his warmth, and only the crown of his head was warm. At about eleven, his second son, named Xiang, and his son-in-law Zhou Changshou, both university graduates who had not believed at first, were struck with wonder.
